preregistration.note: Written before any scoring of the 38 views. Policy numbers below are the docs/quality/a-plus-interior-renders.md section C values and are never tuned. What may change on the TUNING half only: the VLM prompt anchors, the choice of VLM among the pre-listed candidates, the pixel-level definitions marked tunable, and which VLM criteria gate (rule gate_selection). The held-out half is scored once after the rubric is frozen (version 'frozen-*').
preregistration.split_rule: per human grade, order views by sha256(seed:view), deal alternately; odd extras alternate between halves; v27 is forced into tuning because it was shown to three models while probing. Split is computed by archpipe.critic.labels.stratified_split and stored in knowledge/critic/split.json

targets.note: held-out has 8 must_fail and 2 should_pass views, so recall >= 90% means 8/8 and false-fail <= 10% means 0/2. Seeded recall on the audit's QA false passes and on C-or-worse views is also reported.

preregistration.model_note: chosen on the tuning half by the summed gate-selection separation over R5,R7,R8,R9,R10,R11 (scripts/critic_model_compare.py): qwen3.8:27b-mtp-q4_K_M 1.43, gemma4:31b 1.17, qwen3.6:35b-a3b 1.10. The selection rule was written while the first 7 qwen3.8 rows had been read.

scoring.hero_views: all views in the finals set
scoring.hard_fail: a score of 0 on any gating criterion for a hero view
scoring.escalation: two or more gating criteria scored 1 make the view a FAIL
scoring.fail_closed: a criterion that cannot run is not_evaluated; if the VLM is unreachable the verdict is fail with notes.vlm='unavailable'

out_of_scope.R6: texel density needs UV and camera scripts (not an image critic); reported not_evaluated and excluded from the verdict

scoring.gate_selection: a VLM criterion gates iff on the tuning half (fraction of must_fail views scoring < 2) - (fraction of should_pass views scoring < 2) >= 0.30 AND no should_pass view scores 0. Deterministic criteria R1-R4, R10 band/seam, R12 always gate.
scoring.source_cards: every threshold is policy: card ids POLICY-R1 ... POLICY-R13 in knowledge/critic/rubric.json cards

cards.POLICY-R1: R1 lens: 24-35 mm = 2; 16-<24 mm with a written reason in the camera overrides = 1; otherwise 0
cards.POLICY-R2: R2 height: 1.1-1.6 m above the floor datum = 2; within 0.2 m outside = 1; else 0. Floor datums -3.0 m and 0.0 m (camera z minus the highest datum at or below it); documented assumption: render_views.choose eye_m=1.35
cards.POLICY-R3: R3 verticals: |pitch| and vertical-edge deviation <= 0.5 deg = 2; <= 1.5 deg = 1; else 0
cards.POLICY-R4: R4 subject exposure: clipped <= 1 % and crushed <= 2 % of the subject mask = 2; each <= 3x those limits = 1; else 0
cards.POLICY-R10: R10 frame: no solid edge band, no full-height hard seam; near occluder <= 15 %, subject not cropped, empty wall <= 40 %
cards.POLICY-R12: R12 colour: mid-tone opponent excess; cool/cyan/green <= 0.020 and warm <= 0.080 = 2; cool/cyan/green <= 0.040 and warm <= 0.100 = 1; else 0
cards.POLICY-VLM: R5, R7, R8, R9, R10 (occluders, cropping), R11, R13 are judged by the VLM against the anchors in this file, 0/1/2

pixel.subject_mask: union of the camera json 'subjects[].screen' boxes ([x0,y0,x1,y1], y up, fractions of frame; clipped to the frame and flipped to image coordinates). Fallback when no subject box remains or the union covers < 15 % of the frame: central 60 % x 60 % rectangle. Approximation: the boxes are conservative mesh bounds, so the mask is generous and includes background.

vlm.output: {"evidence": string (<= 40 words, name the object and where), "score": 0|1|2}
vlm.pair_rule: R13 runs both left/right orders (benchmark = the cropped 3:2 bedroom-overcast-door.png). Per order: render judged at least as photographic -> 2; benchmark by a slight margin -> 1; by a clear margin -> 0. Final: 2 only if both orders give 2, 0 only if both give 0, otherwise 1.
vlm.preamble: You are a strict but fair architectural-visualisation critic. Image 1 is the REFERENCE render: it is accepted quality and counts as score 2 on every criterion. Image 2 is the render under review. Judge Image 2 on the single criterion below, relative to the reference. Scoring: 2 = as good as the reference, or the problem is absent or minor; 1 = the problem is clearly visible in a noticeable part of Image 2 and worse than in the reference; 0 = the problem is severe, obvious at first glance, large in the frame, and much worse than in the reference. Every render has small flaws, so do not score down for small ones. If you are not sure you can see the problem, score 2. Only describe things you can actually see in Image 2. Reply with JSON only: {"evidence": "<=40 words naming the object and where it is in Image 2", "score": 0|1|2}.

prompts.R5_CONTEXT: Criterion: CONTEXT. What is seen through windows, doors and beyond the building should look like a textured, believable exterior (planting, detailed facades, graded sky). Problems: a window or opening that is a flat white or blank slab, a blank sky slab, neighbouring buildings that are plain white or clay boxes. If no exterior is visible in Image 2, score 2.
prompts.R7_SCALE: Criterion: PHYSICAL SCALE OF MATERIALS. Texture size should match the real material at real size: wood grain, stone veining, tile and paver size. Problems: grain or veins several times too large, blotchy over-coloured marble, stretched or smeared texture mapping, unnatural hue such as salmon-pink timber.
prompts.R8_ASSETS: Criterion: ASSET FIDELITY. How crude are the 3D models. Problems: visible polygon facets on round things (lamp globes, pots), flat card, disc or lollipop shaped foliage, furniture or bedding made of plain boxes, pillows as rigid wedges, clothes like boards. Compare the faceting and crudeness against what the reference shows.
prompts.R9_CONTACT: Criterion: CONTACT AND INTERSECTION. Problems: an object floating with no support, a fitting detached from its wall or ceiling, an object visibly passing through another (cushion through a frame, pillow into a headboard).
prompts.R10_FRAME: Criterion: COMPOSITION AND FRAME INTEGRITY. Problems: something close to the camera blocking more than about 15 percent of Image 2, the main subject cut off by the frame, plain empty wall covering more than about 40 percent, a hard straight vertical or horizontal seam cutting through objects, a dark or solid band along the frame edge, a milky haze or veil, wall or ceiling lines that visibly bend.
prompts.R11_TRUTH: Criterion: TRUTH AND STYLING. Image 2 is titled "{title}". Problems: the picture does not show what the title promises, the room is bare with none of the props that room would have, or the camera looks at the back of furniture. Judge the density of styling against the reference.
prompts.R13_PAIR: Two images follow. Image 1 is labelled A and image 2 is labelled B. One may be a photograph and one may be a computer render. Which one looks more like a real photograph (credible materials, light, imperfection)? Reply with JSON only: {"evidence": "...", "more_photographic": "A"|"B"|"equal", "margin": "clear"|"slight"}.

amendments.why: v0 used red-minus-blue for warm limits, which flags every warm-lit room; the existing render_qa limit is on the cast magnitude. Warm now uses the cast magnitude (<= 0.09 pass, <= 0.10 warn); cool 0.03/0.06, cyan 0.05/0.08; green informational because foliage.
amendments.evidence: tuning half: v0 scored R12=0 on 11 of 20 views including B and B- views with cast 0.065

amendments.why: could not separate the v27 seam (column 609 at 960 px) from real wall edges; the detector is informational, the VLM judges seams; band detector (v19) still gates.
amendments.evidence: tuning half: 7 of 20 views flagged, v27 itself missed

amendments.why: plain gradient median followed foliage and furniture lean; replaced by structure-tensor coherence > 0.9 on strong near-vertical edges with >= 3000 supporting pixels per column bin.
amendments.evidence: tuning half: v0 method gave 2-4 deg on garden views, new method 0.0-0.4 deg except v31 (2.05, slanted panels)

amendments.why: v0 single-image anchors made gemma4:31b score 0 on R7/R8/R9 for 20 of 20 tuning views (B and B- included): no discrimination, 0 hard-fails every good view. v1 scores each criterion relative to the benchmark render shown as a reference (image 1) with severity and extent anchors, and tells the model to score 2 when unsure.
amendments.evidence: tuning half: R8 0/20 >= 1 on every view; R9 0 on 19/20

amendments.why: mixed order results are position bias; final = 2 only when both orders agree the render is at least as photographic, 0 only when both say clearly less, else 1 (text in vlm.pair_rule corrected to match the code written before scoring)
amendments.evidence: none needed; the code was written before the first scoring run
